Epsom College
Welcome to the home of all-round education. Great grades are a given, but your child will learn a whole lot more - about themselves and the world around them - at Epsom College
EXPLORE THE OPPORTUNITIES
Creativity, Art and Culture
We offer all our pupils the benefit of a boarding school routine. That means that every boy and girl has the time to discover their inner artist, musician, performer or designer. Your child will find their creative spark, and we’ll help to keep those fires burning.
Table-toppers
Our winning combination of national titles and sport for all earned Epsom the honour of being named “south east England’s top co-ed school for sport”. That’s because we give as much care and attention to our D, E and F teams as we do to our elite athletes. No matter the level, every child benefits from top coaches and excellent facilities, all delivered on our beautiful 72-acre estate.
The Benefits of Boarding
We’ve offered boarding since 1855 – and a lot’s changed in that time. It’s a traditional model that’s been adapted to suit the needs of the modern family. Longer days, and Saturday lessons, give us time in the week to provide the outstanding all-round education and sporting excellence that we’re famous for.
And with full boarding, weekly boarding, flexible boarding and day options to choose from, there’s something to suit every child and every family.

Director of Quality and International Partnerships
Closing Date 18 September 2026
For further information please see job description below:
08_28-Director-of-Quality-and-International-Partnerships-Job-Description.pdf
Working at Epsom

Drama Awards
We reward pupils who show promise, potential and passion for the dramatic arts, with scholarships at all entry points to the College. Whether you join as a Scholar at 11+, 13+ or 16+, the award is a demonstration of our belief that you are one of our shining lights.
In return, we would expect you to study the subject at GCSE, and A-level where appropriate. Naturally, your commitment to the subject will be outstanding, and we would expect you to be fully involved in the co-curricular drama programme at Epsom College, either on stage as a performer or backstage as part of one of our technical, design or stage management team.
Specific highlights for Drama Scholars include invitation to a varied programme of theatre-related workshops and an annual theatre-themed Drama Scholars’ Dinner.
School Productions
Michaelmas Term
The Senior Play in December offers the first opportunity for Year 10 to Year 13 pupils to participate. In recent years, casts have performed Our Country’s Good, Tartuffe, The Murders at Argos, The Caucasian Chalk Circle, and The Government Inspector.
Lent Term
The Lent Term brings with it the excitement of the Senior Musical, open to pupils from Year 10 to Year 13. Recent productions have included The Addams Family, Shrek, Beauty and the Beast, Footloose and Evita.
Summer Term
There are two Junior Productions in the Summer Term. Year 7 have their own Performing Arts Showcase involving every pupil in a range of singing, acting and dancing numbers. Year 8 and 9 can participate in the Junior Production, which will vary in style each year from straight plays to musical theatre. In recent years, pupils have taken to the stage in productions of Wendy & Peter Pan, The Lion King Jr, The Comedy of Errors, The Sound of Music, Spamalot, Matilda and Philip Pullman’s Grimm Tales.
Aspiring directors are encouraged to hone their skills in the Junior Production with a view to potentially assistant directing shows from Year 10 onwards.
Applying at 11+
To apply for a Drama Scholarship at 11+, you should prepare a monologue that lasts no more than two minutes. You will be expected to perform this ‘in-role’ without using a script. Your monologue should be from a published play, rather than a sketch. It is not necessary to be in costume or bring props, but you may bring simple items if you wish.
Once you have performed your piece, you will participate in a drama workshop involving improvisation activities, and the Director of Drama will speak with you individually. It is optional to bring a portfolio that could help during your discussion with the Director of Drama to illustrate the theatre productions, clubs and classes you have participated in and the performances you have seen.
Assessments will take place in January of Year 6. Assessments for September 2026 entry will take place in January 2026.
Applying at 13+
You can apply either as an actor, or by presenting your theatre design/tech skills. Application forms are sent to all pupils holding a deferred place in the autumn of Year 8.
You should prepare a monologue that lasts no more than two minutes. You will be expected to perform this ‘in-role’ without using a script. Your monologue should be from a published play, rather than a sketch. It is not necessary to be in costume or bring props, but you may bring simple items if you wish.
Once you have performed your piece, you will participate in a drama workshop involving improvisation activities, and the Director of Drama will speak with you individually. It is optional to bring a portfolio that could help during your discussion with the Director of Drama to illustrate the theatre productions, clubs and classes you have participated in and the performances you have seen.
You should present a short demonstration of design from a play of your choice. You may choose to showcase puppetry, masks, sound or set design, makeup, lighting or costume.
Please bring evidence of your work, and talk about your influences, stylistic approach and process. You can use our equipment – such as lighting and soundboards – but please notify us ahead of time if you wish to do this.
It is optional to bring a portfolio that could help during your discussion with the Director of Drama to illustrate, from a design/tech perspective, the theatre productions, clubs and classes you have participated in and the performances you have seen.
The 13+ Drama Scholarship Assessments will take place in the spring of your child’s Year 8.
16+ Scholarships
You can apply either as an actor, or by presenting your theatre design/tech skills. Assessments take place in November of your Year 11.
You should prepare a monologue that lasts no more than two minutes. You will be expected to perform this ‘in-role’ without using a script. Your monologue should be from a published play, rather than a sketch. It is not necessary to be in costume or bring props, but you may bring simple items if you wish.
Once you have performed your piece, you will participate in a drama workshop involving devising and improvisation activities, and the Director of Drama will speak with you individually. It is optional to bring a portfolio that could help during your discussion with the Director of Drama to illustrate the theatre productions, clubs and classes you have participated in and the performances you have seen.
You should present a short demonstration of design from a play of your choice. You may choose to showcase puppetry, masks, sound or set design, makeup, lighting or costume.
Please bring evidence of your work, and talk about your influences, stylistic approach and process. You can use our equipment – such as lighting and soundboards – but please notify us ahead of time if you wish to do this.
It is optional to bring a portfolio that could help during your discussion with the Director of Drama to illustrate, from a design/tech perspective, the theatre productions, clubs and classes you have participated in and the performances you have seen.

Music Awards
The wide-range of opportunities available to our music scholars helps them to secure places at top conservatoires and in national ensembles, and go on to read music at university. We offer scholarships at all entry points, welcoming applications at 11+, 13+ and 16+.
Expectations of a Music Scholar
Award holders are expected to:
In addition to the financial aspect of the award, Music Scholars will receive tuition, free of charge, on one or two instruments.
Regularly attend musical events in school
Study music at least to GCSE level
11+ Scholarships
We look at potential Music Scholars early in the Lent Term of their Year 6.
We are looking for candidates who are at Grade IV on their first instrument (‘instrument’ does include voice). However, if you haven’t quite reached Grade IV, we do consider candidates who show promise and potential.
You will perform two contrasting pieces on your first instrument and a further piece on any other instruments offered. We ask you to sight-read, respond to aural tests and have a brief interview with the Director of Music. We will ask about your musical studies and interests, including any involvement in musical groups or activities.
13+ Scholarships
Pupils applying for a 13+ Music Scholarship will take their assessment early in the Lent Term of their Year 8.
Scholarship application forms are sent to all pupils holding a deferred place in the autumn of their Year 8.
The assessment lasts approximately 25 minutes, with pupils performing three contrasting pieces on their chosen instrument, which may include voice.
Candidates should be of a standard of at least Grade V on their main instrument, or at least Grade VI for pianists.
If you are offering two or more instruments, we will ask you to perform two contrasting pieces on your first instrument and one piece on each of the other instruments.
The 13+ Music Scholarship Assessments will take place in the spring of your child’s Year 8.
All candidates will be asked to sight-read, respond to aural tests, and have a brief interview to discuss their musical studies and interests, including their involvement in musical groups and activities.
16+ Scholarships
As a prospective 16+ Music Scholar, you will be assessed in the Autumn of Year 11, usually in November. You should be at least Grade VIII on your first instrument, which may include voice.
If you’re offering one instrument you will be asked to perform three contrasting pieces of your choice, to sight-read and respond to aural tests.
If you’re offering two or more instruments then you will perform two contrasting pieces on your first instrument and one piece on each of the other instruments, to sight-read and respond to aural tests.
The assessment will conclude with a brief interview with the Director of Music where candidates will be expected to discuss their musical studies and interests, including their involvement in musical groups and activities.

Working at Epsom
Epsom College is one of the UK’s leading independent co-educational schools, providing boarding and day education for 1,100 girls and boys aged 11-18.
The school’s increasing popularity grows out of a rich and distinguished tradition of academic excellence, complemented by a breadth of sporting and cultural opportunities all played out within our beautiful 72-acre estate.
Each person who works at Epsom – whether teaching, coaching, or keeping the school running – plays a vital role in extending the horizons of pupils in a rapidly changing world, while continuing to uphold the College values of kindness, ambition and integrity.

Inspections, Reviews & Awards
The Good Schools Guide
The Good Schools Guide visited in late 2025, and concluded that Epsom is: “a high-achieving, big-hearted and increasingly sought-after school at the top of its game.” Very nice. For the full review, written independently for parents by parents, click below.
Tatler Schools Guide
Tatler has long been an admirer of Epsom College and in 2023, named then-Second Master, Paul Williams, as its “unsung hero of the year” at its annual awards ceremony for his “commitment to education”. In its most recent review of the College, Tatler Schools Guide, said: “Epsom doesn’t rest on the laurels of its reputation on the pitch, but constantly burnishes it.”
The Sunday Times – Parent Power
The go-to league table for parents seeking out their child’s next school. The Sunday Times measures A-levels, GCSEs and a whole load of other metrics to determine who’s up and who’s down in UK education. As with the Good Schools Guide and Tatler (above), these are wholly independent measures of a school’s performance. In the current tables for independent schools (Parent Power 2026 (paywall)) Epsom is 52 in the UK. The year before, when we were 16 places lower, Epsom was judged “Southeast Independent School of the Year”.

Open Mornings & Tours
Our Open Mornings and Tours are the ideal way to see the College, walk the grounds and meet our pupils and staff. You can book your visit or read some frequently asked questions below.
Open Morning
Our Open Mornings take place twice a year on Saturday mornings. Once in the autumn and spring. They offer a comprehensive introduction to our College and feature:
The Head’s welcome presentation
Departmental showcases and activities
Tours of the College with current pupils
Conversations with staff and students

Any Questions?
What's the difference between each of the events?
Open Mornings
Open Mornings are the ideal introduction and overview of the College. These flagship events feature departmental showcases and a talk from the Head. They take place on Saturday morning.
You will get to see: buildings, classrooms, departmental showcases, sports facilities, our grounds, the Lower School and a day or boarding house.
College Tours
College Tours are smaller and take place on weekday mornings throughout the academic year. You will see the school on a normal working morning – with lessons rather than showcases and no formal presentation from the Head.
Private Visits
Bespoke in nature, these tours are designed for families with specific questions who seek a more tailored experience. After a short tour and the chance to visit one of our boarding or day houses, you will have a one-to-one meeting with the Head.
When's the best time to see the College?
Year 7 & Year 9 applications
You’ll need to register by the October of your child’s Year 6. Therefore we recommend looking around when your child is in Year 5 (sometimes Year 4 if you’re really keen).
We would recommend coming with your child so that they also get a feel for the College and our pupils.
Year 7 admissions Year 9 admissions
Year 12 applications
The best time to see the College if you’re considering applying to our Sixth Form will be in Year 10, as the registration deadline is mid-October in Year 11.
Should I bring my child?
Absolutely! Whichever school your child ultimately joins, it’s important that they will be happy there. We believe that they also settle best when they feel they have been involved in making the choice.
However, you are equally welcome to attend any of our events without your child. We know many parents appreciate the chance to get a feel for the College themselves before involving their child in the process.
All of our events are tailored to prospective pupils, so we hope they will get plenty from the visit.
We provide each family with their own pupil guide, who will be close in age to your child. We hope this means that your child will remain engaged during their visit and feel able to ask questions.
Can I contact the Admissions Team?
Our Admissions team are available all year round to answer any questions you may have. Simply get in touch by phone or email, using the contact details below.

Reaching Out & Building Partnerships
We work in partnership with a number of schools, charities, community projects and NGOs. Our aim is to create meaningful and beneficial opportunities for those we work with. We share our facilities, resources, knowledge and experience so that as many people as possible can reach their true potential.
Primary Schools
We partner with over 100 local primary and prep schools each year. Our outreach programme sees teachers visiting schools to take lessons, conduct scientific experiments, lead drama workshops and run art classes.
Our senior pupils support primary-age pupils with literacy and numeracy, they help them to take their first steps with modern languages, and even design and build sensory play equipment in their DT lessons.
We also invite Year 4 and 5 children to the College, to access our facilities and enjoy any number of activities such as our weekly sports masterclasses, science days, public speaking events and sports tournaments – such as the huge cross country event, or the Nat Sciver Sheild for Girls’ Cricket.
Our music and drama workshops see children from a number of schools come to the College, learn new pieces from scratch and then perform to parents in an end-of-day extravaganza (pictured).
Secondary Schools
Over the years we have developed sustained, meaningful partnerships with a number of secondary schools and Sixth Form Colleges in the region. Each of these is built on an exchange of innovative best practice, and a sharing of knowledge, resources and opportunities.
Highlights include our long-standing work with colleagues in the Bourne Education Trust, a partnership of 16 schools throughout Surrey and Hampshire.
We also helped to fund, launch and staff the Invicta Academy, an online ‘pop-up’ school offering catch-up lessons to pupils from disadvantaged parts of Surrey whose education suffered during the Covid pandemic.
Aspiring Oxbridge candidates from schools across Surrey are also supported by the College. We help to guide their applications, giving advice on personal statements and providing one-to-one support for interviews.
We also partnered with Motorsport UK to deliver a day dedicated to getting more girls interested in STEM. Epsom pupils worked with girls from a number of local schools to take on pit stop challenges, science experiments and even try their hand at broadcasting (pictured).
Opening Our Doors
We also work with third parties to widen access to education – including an innovative scheme run by Hockey Inner City (HIC). This is a venture aimed at improving access to hockey for children from backgrounds traditionally under-represented in the sport.
HIC approached Epsom and we were delighted to help. We provided our facilities and top coaches for a day of masterclasses that focused on shooting, dribbling and elimination, defending and ball control. Click the video to learn more.
Our Drama department is privileged enough to have access to a number of fantastic opportunities through London theatres, including the National Theatre’s New Views playwrighting programme. Whenever these opportunities arise, we invite students from local schools to join us so that they too can benefit from these experiences.

Design & Technology
Traditional techniques fuse with state-of-the-art equipment in large, purpose-built studios. Design & technology is where our future designers and engineers first found creative ways to solve real-world problems.
Design & technology gives our pupils the opportunity to develop practical, spatial and intuitive intelligence. They become critical thinkers, problem solvers and young entrepreneurs. By harnessing practical skills and creative thinking in a variety of materials and technologies, we encourage and support our pupils to think big and design bold.
Our links with industry involve factory tours, presentations from leaders in their field, and access to many of London’s leading exhibitions, galleries, tradeshows and museums. A number of our pupils have gone on to careers in architecture, product design, gaming and engineering.
Technologically Advanced
The Design & Technology building combines the very latest technology with traditional tools and materials. Whether it’s hand-crafted or cutting edge, computer-aided or spot-welded, our pupils enjoy some of the best-specced studio space of any school in the country.
Our two design studios, two workshops, CNC Suite, Machine Room and Exhibition Display area are equipped with a comprehensive range of traditional and high-tech machinery, including:
40 computers packed with professional software
A3 and 3D scanners
Wacom Touchscreens
Two engineers’ lathes
Milling machine
Three pillar drills
Wood lathes
Hot metals work area
Brazing hearths
MIG welders
Excel router
Pewter casting and enamelling kit
Laser cutter
Unimatic router
Plastics forming equipment
Roland CAMM vinyl cutter
Large circular saw
Planer thicknesser
Table router
Academic Study
From Year 7 to Year 9 all pupils study design & technology through small project work. They design and build torches, bug hotels, storage boxes and MP3 speaker docks. They learn pewter casting, CAD, laser cutting, dovetail joint work, and a range of other skills and processes. All of which builds confidence in the workshop, develops theoretical knowledge in the classroom, and readies pupils for the challenge and fulfilment of GCSE and A-levels.
The GCSE and A-level programme develops pupils’ ability to design and build prototypes that solve real-world problems. We focus on the origin and quality of ideas, paying attention to form, function, user needs and sustainability. Pupils work individually, and within groups, producing work that is often award-winning and market-ready.
STEM Electric Race Cars
As part of our co-curricular STEM offering, where design & technology combines with science, maths and computer science, our pupils have designed and built battery-powered electric race cars to compete at Goodwood Race Course.
Pitting their wits against schools, colleges and universities from around the UK, our pupils designed and constructed the chassis, bodywork, drive chain and electrical control systems. They raced in practice sessions around the College grounds, and then modified and refined their designs further.
On race day, our Sixth Form team finished fifth out of a field of 30; with our Year 10 & 11 team coming 18th.

Careers & Higher Education
Every pupil receives first-class guidance for their journey into life beyond Epsom. Our Careers and Higher Education programme begins in a pupil’s first year, and continues as part of their PSHE curriculum. The support increases as pupils move into Year 11 and they start to focus more intently on university destinations, personal statements and relevant work experience.
Year 11
In their final GCSE year, all pupils take part in the Morrisby Careers Programme. Pupils take part in psychometric testing and aptitude profiling, alongside detailed discussions about their interests and academic ability, that involves parents, pastoral staff and academic tutors.
Based on all of the above, each pupil’s individual Morrisby Profile provides detailed guidance and advice on A-level choices and university pathways.
Once GCSEs are over, pupils are encouraged to seek work experience during the long summer break. The aim is to gain useful and relevant knowledge and skills that may help university applications, or provide useful insight to aid career choices.
Support in Lower Sixth
From ‘World of Work’ evenings, interview training, careers tasters and a varied programme of webinars, seminars and insights into different professions and industries, students access a structured programme of expert careers advice and guidance in Year 12.
This is also the year when university applications are made, and students will be given tailored one-to-one support throughout. Whether that’s UCAS, Oxbridge, medicine or applications to leading US and international universities. We host a Higher Education Conference and Fair in the Summer Term, which is attended by most top universities and features workshops from admissions tutors.
We even provide support to those pupils who want to gain greater life experience before entering higher education – with ideas for gap years and apprenticeships.
Students are inducted into Unifrog, an online platform that guides students through the university application process, and alternative pathways. Parents also have the opportunity to log-in and can access Unifrog by clicking here.
Support in the Upper Sixth
At the start of Year 13, students are supported in fine-tuning their university applications and personal statements. They receive interview preparation and coaching as required, and students will usually seek the support of subject specialists. We also invite university students and admissions tutors to give talks on student finance and mental wellbeing at university.
Once offers start coming in, guided support is available to help students make informed choices ahead of A-level results day. And – on the big day itself – Heads of Department are available for every student who has missed their grades.
While the vast majority of students get the grades they want and achieve their first choice university, those who miss out will be given every possible assistance. There is immediate advice on hand: whether to re-mark, who to call, whether to look at Clearing, and so on. There is a workshop in September to assist and support any student who needs to begin the UCAS process again.
Careers Handbook
For detailed guidance on the support available throughout the whole of your child’s time at Epsom, you can download the Careers Handbook.
Careers Bulletin
We produce a Careers Bulletin five times a year. This comprehensive round-up of the latest opportunities and advice for the world of work is made available to all pupils and parents. Click below to access the most recent edition.

Our Governors
Alex Russell OBE
Alex Russell OBE has an MA (Hons) in History from the University of Edinburgh. He gained his teaching qualification from University College London (Institute of Education).
Following two successful headships, Alex established Bourne Education Trust in 2013 to work with schools in challenging circumstances. As CEO, he has grown the Trust from 2 to 36 schools over the last 13 years. It now covers all school phases and includes primary, secondary and special schools as well as those providing alternative provision for pupils outside of mainstream education.
Alex is a National Leader of Education, leads Surrey County Council’s inclusion roundtable and in 2023 co-founded the charity, AI in Education, which helps schools and colleges to embed AI safely, ethically and effectively. In 2021, Alex was awarded an OBE for services to education.
Karen Thomas
Karen Thomas is the Vice Chair of the Board of Governors and the Chair of the Royal Medical Foundation of Epsom College and an ex-parent. She is a retired Orthopaedic Surgeon. During her career she set up a clinical network serving Surrey and West Sussex and held local, regional and national leadership roles. Karen’s most important commitment was in the field of postgraduate surgical education and supporting the next generation of surgeons. Her contributions to clinical practice, medical leadership and postgraduate surgical education have had a lasting impact on the healthcare community in the UK.
Karen sits on several School Board of Governors in the local area for multi academy trust schools and chairs the governing board of a school for children and young people with special needs.
Seema Bains
Educated at Tiffin Girls’ School, Seema obtained her law degree from Kingston University. Seema qualified as a solicitor in 1997 and since 2009 she has been a Partner at DWF, a leading global provider of integrated legal and business services representing insurers and large corporates in insurance claims.
Beyond her legal practice, Seema serves as the Head of DWF’s Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Leadership Group, where she has been instrumental in fostering an inclusive culture within the firm. Her efforts in promoting gender diversity have been recognised, notably with her inclusion in the 2020 and 2021 “HERoes Top 100 Women Executives List,” which showcases leaders driving change for gender diversity in the workplace.
Sarah Blaney
Educated at Epsom between 2001-2003, Sarah studied Geography at University College London before obtaining a first-class law degree at BPP in London. After training, qualifying and practising as an energy lawyer at City law firm CMS Cameron McKenna Nabarro Olswang LLP before working as a senior lawyer for an oil major for a number of years. She is now Of Counsel at a large City law firm, advising on corporate and commercial matters, and is a mother of young twin daughters.
John Bowerman
John was educated at Epsom College from 1969-1974 and went on to read Philosophy, Politics and Economics (PPE) at Christ Church, Oxford.
After initially working in management consulting for Arthur Andersen, John changed to pursue a career in commercial real estate, qualifying as a Chartered Surveyor in 1986. Specialising in corporate real estate since then, John worked for Richard Ellis (now CBRE), Credit Suisse and Barclays Capital, advising on and managing occupational and data centre real estate requirements, being based at various times in London, Tokyo and Hong Kong. John is now with State Street Bank & Trust Co in London where he leads its EMEA real estate team, responsible for the Bank’s occupational property portfolio across the region.
Married to Gill, a Registered General Nurse in primary care, John has three sons. His interests include sport, music, film and art.
Tania Botting
Tania Botting was Headmistress of Greenfield School, a co-educational preparatory school in Woking. Tania has worked in a variety of different schools, both within the independent and maintained sectors during her 30-year career.
Tania was educated at Nonsuch High School before completing her Bachelor of Education at the University of Winchester. Tania completed a Masters in Educational Leadership in 2015. Tania Botting was appointed Chair of IAPS from August 2024 and Vice Chair of ISC from March 2025. The Independent Association of Prep Schools (IAPS) is a membership body offering guidance and advice to Heads and their schools. IAPS membership is a marker of excellence amongst prep schools and parents, ensuring best practice and the highest standards of education. Founded in 1892, it is the largest Heads Association within the Independent Schools Council (ISC), with over 660 member schools.
John Hay
John Hay was educated in Glasgow and moved to London to pursue a career in journalism. He spent 15 years working on newspapers and business magazines before making the move into PR and advertising with two of the UK’s ‘Top 20’ agencies.
He subsequently set up a full-service marketing communications consultancy, running it for 10 years before retiring in 2018. Both his son and his daughter attended Epsom College.
Ashley Head
Ashley Head’s 30-year corporate career has seen him occupy the roles of senior vice president at Chase Manhattan Bank; and senior vice-president at Mastercard International. He has also built and sold four companies, including Datacash – a top 50 AIM company – which he sold to Mastercard in 2010.
Ashley also supports many charities and is a Trustee of The National Emergencies Trust and an Ambassador to The Childrens Trust.
Dej Mahoney
Dej became a Governor in 2016, having previously been a Member of Council. He’s a proud OE, a former Head of School and a Cambridge law graduate who was called to the Bar of England and Wales as a Harmsworth Award winner. He is a founding director of All Our Business Ltd (AOB), a legal and business consultancy in music and entertainment. Through AOB, Dej became a founding director of the Barclaycard World Freerun Championships and a founding director of Young Voices International.
Previously, Dej was a VP at Sony Music. During that time, he was a visiting lecturer at the University of Westminster, a contributing author of Digitisation and the Music Industry and became a Member of the Mayor’s Creative Commission for London. He is on the Governing Board of the BRIT School of the Performing Arts. In 2018, Dej was seconded to the Senior Management Team at Warner Chappell Music and in 2020, he was appointed as the first Non-Executive Chairman of West One Music Group.
Julian Mount
Julian held the position of Managing Director, Alliance Healthcare UK, the UK’s largest pharmaceutical wholesaler, from 2017-2022. Leading a team of more than 5,500 employees across 11 business units, distributing pharmaceuticals and medical services to community pharmacies, hospitals and homes across the UK.
Raised in Nigeria, Julian returned to the UK to study Electrical & Electronic Engineering before embarking on a career in Global healthcare management. A seasoned industry expert, with experience domestically and across five continents, Julian has worked in healthcare, supply chain and bio-tech businesses. His roles have included European Vice President and European Leadership Team member at Pfizer, and International Vice President at Alexion Pharmaceuticals. In his most recent role, Julian was responsible for the UK roll-out of the COVID vaccination program delivering over 45 million doses.
Anish Patel
Anish joined the Board of Governors in March 2023. He is an OE (Robinson House 1998-2003) with an MA in Mathematics from Cambridge University and an MBA from Stanford University.
Having started his career at L.E.K. Consulting and Barclays, Anish is now a private investor and advisor to private-equity-backed companies. Anish is passionate about the transformative potential of technology in education, and sits on the Board of multiple education-related organisations, including as Chair of a MAT secondary school.
Nicky Sinker
Nicky Sinker studied Economics at Warwick University before qualifying as a chartered accountant.
She spent the majority of her career in Business Management/COO roles within Financial Services and Legal, helping business with setting and execution of strategy, governance, risk management, cost reduction/management and project management. Ultimately driving constant improvements in the way they worked whilst improving profitability.
She now specializes in sustainability, helping organisations reduce their climate impact whilst improving their profitability and ability to win more work. She is the mother of twin daughters.
Alex Vartevanian
Educated at Epsom College from 2006-2011, Alex studied Management at the University of Nottingham before starting accountancy at KPMG, qualifying as a Chartered Accountant in 2019.
Alex worked at KPMG for over seven years, initially as a member of the Technology, Media and Telecoms audit team before joining the Energy Deal Advisory team. Alex is now working at investment banking firm Moelis & Company advising on transactions across a broad range of industries and products including M&A, restructuring, capital markets and financial institutions advisory.
Alex is also a governor and chairs the Finance and Resources Committee at Esher Church of England High School.
Sarah Whyatt
Educated at Bradford Grammar School before graduating with an MEng in Manufacturing engineering from Durham University. After qualifying as a Chartered Accountant at Deloitte, Sarah then spent the next 20 years of her career at an oil major.
Working in a variety of different finance roles, specialising in financial planning and performance management. Most recently, Sarah has been working to provide leadership and operational delivery of sustainability disclosure requirements. Married to David, Sarah has a son and a daughter.
Organisation and management
The Board of Governors generally meet three times a year for routine matters and also for one full day together to discuss the Governors’ and Head’s vision for the College. This provides an opportunity for the Board to focus on particular areas to consider, develop and monitor the College’s strategic direction.
There are, in addition, four permanent sub-committees comprised of Governors and the Senior Leadership Team, that meet at least once a term:
Safeguarding and Pastoral
Education
Finance and Infrastructure
Risk & Revenue Sub-Committee
Training
New Governors are inducted into the workings of the College, both as a company and as a charity, by being invited to attend all of the sub-committee meetings as observers in their first year of appointment. In addition, they are provided with guidance from the Charity Commission, AGBIS (Association of Governing Bodies of Independent Schools) and ISC (Independent Schools Council). They are also provided with relevant updates and given the opportunity to attend relevant training courses throughout the year.
Contacting the Chair of Governors
Anyone wishing to contact the Chair of Governors should do so in writing. Please direct all communication to:
Mr Alex Russell, Chair of the Governors, c/o The Bursar’s Office, Epsom College, College Road, Epsom, Surrey KT17 4JQ.
The proprietor is Epsom College Ltd. Epsom College is a company limited by guarantee and is a subsidiary charity of The Royal Medical Foundation of Epsom College. The Council of the parent charity, The Royal Medical Foundation of Epsom College (RMF of EC), appoints and removes the Governors of Epsom College and delegates roles and duties for the strategic management and development of the College to the Governors of Epsom College. The Board of Governors reports to the Council of the RMF of EC.
Epsom College Board of Governors, who are also the Charity Trustees and the directors of the charitable company Epsom College, are selected from a wide range of backgrounds, and the aim is to achieve a balanced Board with a core of individuals with educational, legal, risk, accountancy, finance, property management, business, marketing and pastoral backgrounds. All share a genuine commitment to the future of the College. The Chair of Epsom College Board of Governors is Mr Alex Russell OBE.

Academic Scholarships
Scholarships and Exhibitions are awarded to pupils who excel academically. They are prestigious, and our scholars go on to contribute much to the life of Epsom College. Pupils are awarded at each entry point to the College – 11+, 13+ and 16+ – with awards ranging in value from £750 to £6,000 per year.
What’s Involved in Being a Scholar?
A pupil’s award lasts throughout their time at the College, subject to certain standards and expectations being met. Scholars must review their performance twice a year, and explain in writing how they remain a worthy recipient of their award. All Scholars are expected to:
Display an outstanding attitude to learning
Rewarding Progress
Any pupil who misses out on securing a scholarship is able to reapply at the next entry point. Therefore an unsuccessful candidate at Year 7, is encouraged to try again at Year 9 or Year 12. At every stage we wish to reward the talents of all pupils and celebrate their progress. Previous record is no impediment.
11+ Scholarships
At this entry point, you do not have to apply for an academic scholarship.
Children in Year 6 are already under great pressure, and sit many exams. We do not wish to add to this by making them sit any more.
We’re confident our admissions process is able to identify the talent, potential and promise of each child.
11+ Academic Scholarships are therefore awarded on the strength of the entrance exams, engagement day and supporting school references.
13+ Scholarships
Applicants must demonstrate a high level of all-round academic performance and potential. Candidates will take part in:
academic scholarship: English Sample Paper
Academic Scholarship: mathematics sample paper
ACADEMIC SCHOLARSHIP: TASK DESCRIPTORS
Scholarship assessments for pupils joining Year 9 in September 2026 will take place March, 2026.
written tests in English and Mathematics
16+ Scholarships
To be awarded a scholarship at 16+, pupils must have excellent predicted grades at GCSE or IGCSE and submit exceptional school reports and references, with evidence of outstanding effort.
Candidates will attend a two-hour session at the College, consisting of:
ACADEMIC SCHOLARSHIP: TASK DESCRIPTORS
Scholarship assessments for those looking to join Epsom in September 2026 will take place on Wednesday 12 November, 2025.

Sports Awards
We want you to bring your talent and ability to our College, and we welcome applications from potential Sports Scholars at all entry points: 11+, 13+ and 16+.
Sport is central to life at Epsom, and we have long been recognised for our sporting achievements. Already, this year, we have won national titles in shooting, hockey, rugby, squash, cricket and golf. And our alumni have represented their countries in the Olympics, Cricket World Cup finals and the Six Nations.
Benefits
Our Sports Scholars become part of our Talented and Gifted programme, accessing specialist coaching and 1-1 tuition, alongside personalised strength and conditioning work. Scholars will also access our links with many professional teams, and benefit from pathway programmes to elite-level competition.
Expectations
We want all our pupils to access sport, and to enjoy it, regardless of ability. We would expect Scholars to play a central role in ensuring this happens.
You will also be required to represent the College in your chosen sport on a regular basis – ideally across all three terms. You are expected to train and compete for your teams during periods of study leave, school holidays and after public exams. All the while embodying the qualities we hold dear: empathy, confidence, creativity, determination, self-discipline and excellence.
11+ and 13+ Scholarships
Potential Sports Scholars are assessed the school year before they are due to start at Epsom.
Physical & Motor Skills
First, we assess physical and motor skills. This takes place at Epsom. Candidates should bring suitable indoor trainers and their current school’s PE Kit.
Sport-Specific Assessment
Pupils are asked to choose two sports from the following list, indicating which they specialise in:
We approach the child’s school for a reference and ask candidates to supply external references and testimonials with their application. We’re keen to hear about the child’s ability, coachability, potential, commitment and self-discipline.
We are not able to assess sports which are not listed above.

If your sport isn’t on the list above please don’t be put off. We do consider applications from candidates who demonstrate exceptional talent in other sports.
Shortlisted applicants will be asked to attend a coaching session at Epsom, and we do try to observe a coaching session at their own club or academy. We may also seek references from your external coaches.

Drama
Drama holds a special place in the hearts of everyone at Epsom. Throughout the year – whether in academic lessons, co-curricular clubs and productions or house-based events – drama entertains, educates and enlightens. Our pupils take centre stage and work wonders backstage to ensure that drama remains one of the most cherished aspects of College life.
Showstoppers
We stage four major productions each year, which provide pupils with the opportunity to perform on stage or take part as a member of the band for musical theatre performances. For those who enjoy working behind the scenes, production roles are plentiful – including stage managers, costume designers, sound technicians, lighting and special effects operators, props and set designers.
Every Year 7 pupil participates in a weekly Performing Arts Carousel over the course of the year, they all perform in their Summer Performing Arts Showcase. Pupils in Year 8 and 9 have the chance to be in the Junior Production, and pupils from Year 10 to Year 13 can choose from the annual Senior Play and Senior Musical.
These productions are large scale with close to 300 pupils in total involved across the year. Performances take place in front of sell-out audiences – including matinees for local schools.
Cultural Highlights
The development of skills, such as collaboration, confidence and creativity, is a crucial part of the dramatic process, and we encourage this further through clubs, theatre trips and a programme of drama workshops, often involving visiting professional practitioners. GCSE and A-level pupils also have the opportunity to sample the theatrical delights of New York on an exciting biennial trip.
We support pupils in their application to prestigious organisations, such as National Youth Theatre, and have an excellent track record of success in LAMDA examinations (Acting, Reading for Performance or Public Speaking).
As well as gaining places in the National Youth Theatre and performance opportunities at Edinburgh Fringe with the Young Pleasance, our pupils have taken roles in West End plays such as Moana, and on major TV dramas, including The Crown.
Clubs & Societies
Right from the start of Year 7, all the way to the Upper Sixth, there are clubs and societies that will deepen our pupils’ love of theatre and performance.
Aspiring stage designers and technicians can sign up for Junior or Senior Theatre Design and Tech Club, while those wanting to expand their performance skills and experience can take part in Junior Drama Club. The clubs for younger pupils are often led or assisted by senior Drama students, which helps to build confidence and foster strong bonds between pupils of different ages and abilities.

Music
Music is integral to the life of our school, giving pupils skills and experiences that stay with them for the rest of their lives.
Our aim is to enable every pupil to experience the best and widest range of music-making, whether as a performer or listener. We approach this by sharing a love of music across the School, and by inspiring pupils to achieve – for themselves – the highest possible standards.
Beyond music as a curriculum subject, we encourage co-curricular participation for every pupil who is interested and able. From the rock band to the chamber choir and with a lively calendar of concerts and performances, we cater for the widest possible range of tastes, expectations and experiences. The diverse range of places where pupils can make music, practise, listen to and compose it, makes Epsom very special indeed.
“Pupils flourish due to the range of opportunities available, the supportive attitude of their peers, and the direction of inspirational staff”
Choral Music
All pupils are involved in singing, whether it be hearty hymn-singing in the Chapel or the fiercely-contested house choral competition. This culture is established right at the outset with all new Lower School pupils singing in the Third Form choir.
The Chapel choirs lead the music in Chapel each week, and for special services. They cover an extensive repertoire of sacred music and are given opportunities to perform outside school, including regular cathedral visits and tours abroad.
The chamber choir gives our senior choristers the chance to explore a more complex repertoire and experience workshops with professional choirs. Many of our singers are members of national youth choirs and take up choral scholarships at universities.
Instrumental Music
There are numerous opportunities for instrumentalists at the College, whether through larger-scale ensembles or our chamber music programme. We provide two ensembles within each area of music-making; one that allows musicians to gain experience and another that stretches our leading musicians.
Our scholarship programme encourages musicians to participate regularly in chamber music, and they have regular meetings with staff to discuss performance opportunities and their general progress; while the broader programme is tailor-made each year to the needs and abilities of our pupils, to provide them with a host of enriching musical opportunities.
Contemporary and Music Technology
Whether it be rock groups or close harmony singing, there are myriad opportunities for non-classical music-making. The department runs several band workshops led by our visiting music staff helping them both perform and write their own songs.
The College has recently invested in high specification recording studio which gives pupils opportunities to get involved with music recording and production.
Pupils have the opportunity to work with and learn from our full-time head of music technology, who has a wealth of professional experience within the recording industry.
Jazz
Jazz is increasingly popular at Epsom with highlights including our annual jazz night and performances at professional jazz clubs.
We have designed a programme that allows pupils to develop as jazz musicians throughout their time at the College. Lower School have a junior blues ensemble which introduces pupils to the art of improvisation. This programme continues into the Senior School with an inclusive jazz ensemble and the auditioned big band.

OE Clubs, Chapters & Societies
Membership of the OE Club opens up access to a wide-range of Chapters, Societies and Clubs. These professional networks, and social and sporting clubs, benefit long-established members as well as those about to embark upon the first stage of their careers.
Reflecting Epsom’s global outlook, and in recognition of the fact that not everyone is able to return to KT17, the OE Club holds regular events around the world.
Professional Societies
Pupils at the College are encouraged to participate in various events, hosted by the OE Professional Societies, in order to develop their communication skills and advance their thinking about a future career.
If you have any questions or comments about our professional societies, or are able to offer careers advice and/or work experience, please get in touch.
For more information on the Professional Societies, click on the headings below.
Banking & Financial Services Society
OEs working in all areas of finance are welcome to join the Society. Networking drinks receptions are held in London pubs and other venues and if you are able to host a drinks reception at your place of work, please click here to contact the OE Club.
Join the OE Banking & Financial Services Society’s LinkedIn group or get in touch for more information.
Legal Society
Officially formed in 2009 by Steven Kay QC (P 1968-73), one of the key aims of the Legal Society is to create a network of help and support for young people starting out among the great number of solicitors and barristers associated with Epsom College.
Join the OE Legal Society’s LinkedIn group or get in touch for more information.
Medical Society
Established in 2000 by Paul Knapman (W 1958-63), the OE Medical Society welcomes those involved in the medical, dental, veterinary, pharmaceutical and medical science professions.
The current President of the Society is Bryan Mayou (P 1958-1963).
The Society’s aims are to create a professional network for its members and provide a network of support for young OEs starting out in this range of professions, as well as students contemplating these careers.
Every year, the Society holds an annual dinner in central London venues associated with medicine, or at the College. The Medical Society also gets together for an informal drinks gathering bi annually.
To read about the College’s medical history, see Medical Excellence: The Early Years by Dr John Ford (Fa1950-55).
Join the OE Medical Society’s LinkedIn group or get in touch for more information.
Property & Associated Services Society
Membership of the OE Property & Associated Services Society, launched in 2013, represents a wide cross-section of property interests, ranging from finance to design.
The aim of the society is to create a professional network for its members and provide valuable career advice to current students and young OEs.
Join the OE Property and Associated Services Society’s LinkedIn group or get in touch for more information.
Sports Clubs & Societies
Expertise in a particular sport is not always essential to joining and all clubs are very keen to recruit new members. Ideas for new Clubs and Societies are always welcome.
For more information about our current Sports Clubs and Societies please click the headings below.
Classic Car Club
The OE Classic Car Club (OECCC) got off to a flying start on Founder’s Day 2018, with over 20 vehicles turning up to create a wonderful display.
Classic and vintage car owners come out in force each year at Founder’s Day and are a great attraction for the many visitors to the College.
For more information on the OECCC please contact Director of Development, Helen Tranter.
Cricket
A relaxed, friendly atmosphere coupled with a fierce competitive edge is the style of the OE Cricket Club.
A series of lively fixtures is organised against good club sides during the season and includes the annual match against the College 1st XI. All matches are played on immaculate grounds and followed by a post-match social.
OEs, male or female, of any age and playing ability, are welcome to join. If you would like to get involved, please contact Harry Williams (P 2011-16).
Football
The OE Football Club (OEFC) plays in the Arthurian League and in three cup competitions:
OEFC also have an annual match against the College XI. Over the course of a season, the club will fulfil up to 25 fixtures. Our home ground is Tolworth Goals (Deckers Sports Ground), Tolworth, KT5 9NT.
Away fixtures take place in the London and Greater London area.
We are keen to recruit more players to grow the club and increase the number of fixtures per season, there are plenty of opportunities for new players to get involved. If you would like to take part, please contact Alistair Morris.
Instagram: www.instagram.com/old_epsomians
The Arthur Dunn
Junior League Cup
Lord David Woolcott Trophy
Golf
The Old Epsomian Golf Society has an impressive membership of all ages and standards. Many handicap matches, prestigious scratch tournaments and putting competitions are held throughout the year against other Societies, the Common Room and the College.
In 2017, the Society was delighted to win the two major titles, the coveted Halford Hewitt Cup and Grafton Morrish competition.
The Society looks forward to welcoming both female and male members and is confident all OEs will enjoy the opportunity to extend their game, while renewing old acquaintances and making new ones.
For more details, contact Adam Maurice.
Rifle Club
The OE Rifle Club (OERC) encourages OEs to further their marksmanship skills and enjoy many lively social occasions.
Competing at national and county level, the OERC offers opportunities for everyone to compete – from beginners to advanced shooters. Practices and team shoots are scheduled every two weeks during the season, which runs from March to the end of July.
The highlight of the calendar is the Imperial Meeting in July, commencing with the Ashburton Veterans and culminating ten days later with the final of the Queen’s prize.
Many OERC members regularly represent GB, England or Scotland in the Olympics and Commonwealth Games and are always happy to assist others with international-level coaching. For more information contact the OE Club
To learn more about the history of Shooting at the College, click here
The 50 Club
The 50 Club was founded in 2013-14 with the intention of raising funds to help support pupils in the Target Rifle Shooting squad at Epsom College.
Members of the Club make an annual standing order donation of £50 with 50% of donations going towards shooting equipment for that year. Each member’s name then goes into a prize draw, which takes place at the Ashburton Dinner in June and the remaining 50% of the donations is divided between four winners.
For more details about becoming a member of the 50 Club, please contact the OE team.
Special thanks go to Peter Dodd (Rosebery 1943-47) and Andrew Lothian (Forest 1969-74) who started this initiative.
Squash
Informal squash matches are held at the College and an OE Squash Team is entered into the prestigious Londonderry Cup.
Please contact Tim Abbott if you are interested in playing.
Our Overseas Chapters
Click the headings below to find out more about each overseas chapter.
Australia
President of the OE Australian Chapter, Michael Diamond (Rn 1984-89), who lives in St Ives in NSW, would be delighted to hear from any OEs residing in Australia, as well as those passing through.
Mark Hohenberg (Rn 1994-99) and Ravinder Sehmi (Fa 1982-87) head up the Sydney branch.
Annual lunches are held in Sydney and Melbourne.
During her visit to Australia in 2023, Director of Development, Helen Tranter, was delighted to meet a number of OEs who showed great enthusiasm for increased OE connectivity.
Hong Kong
The Chapter was launched officially at a Reception in Hong Kong in October 2017.
The OE community in Hong Kong is the largest outside the UK and Helen Tranter, Director of Development, has enjoyed meeting many OEs and Epsom College parents at drinks receptions, dinners, a wine tasting and a family brunch.
The Chapter Committee endeavours to meet regularly and organise a range of events for OEs. These include a get-together at a race meet and lunches for the Chapter’s networking societies.
For further information, contact the President of the Chapter, Justin Lau (G 1990-95).
Malaysia & Singapore
The OE Malaysia and Singapore Chapter includes former students from both Epsom College in the UK and Epsom College in Malaysia.
The Chapter is building a vibrant alumni network that will support OEs through their career, as well as create a strong social group with regular events.
For further information contact Andrew Diamond (P 1987-90)
North America
The US Chapter is led by Bill Fleming (Propert 1956-58), who lives on the East Coast.
The Canadian Chapter is led by Simon Law (Rosebery 1984-89).

Clubs, Societies & Activities
Our pupils want to be rounded, experienced and world-ready. We want to help them. That’s why each day, once lessons are over, all our pupils take part in our award-winning co-curricular programme. There are over 150 clubs, societies and activities to choose from, helping pupils to find like minds, new experiences and fresh challenges.
Breadth of Opportunity
We don’t pigeonhole our pupils, and we don’t want them to limit themselves. That’s why – in Years 7, 8 and 9 – the co-curricular programme is a combination of ‘free choice’ activities, and a carousel of experiences that pupils engage with on rotation.
Choices extend from the academic and cultural to the physical, ensuring that pupils stretch mind as well as muscle.
In the Senior years – Year 10 and above – pupils take on leadership roles. They work alongside younger pupils – for example, by directing plays – or they lead the academic societies.
And if a burning passion isn’t sated by what’s on offer, pupils can bid to start their own society. The Climate Committee, Amnesty International and the Diversity, Equality and Inclusivity Society are just a few recent examples.
Many of our clubs offer opportunities to compete in national competitions. The STEM Club, for example, competes each year in the UK Rocketry Competition, and races electric cars against schools, universities and youth groups at the Goodwood Race Course (pictured).
Award-Winning Choice and Opportunity
Our co-curricular programme has won multiple awards in recent years. Recognised by The Week magazine as ‘the best of the best’ within independent education, pupils are spoilt for choice with more on offer than they could ever reasonably expect to experience.
The lists below give you an idea of what is available throughout the academic year. Please note, that this is the full range of activities on offer throughout the year. Not all options are available to every year group, or during every term.

Supporting Epsomians at The Start of Their Careers
We are grateful to all the OEs who have supported current pupils and young OEs as they develop their careers. Advice about where to go next is essential when planning for future employment, and work experience not only gives pupils insight into a possible career, but improves their knowledge and understanding of the skills required by employers.
Benefiting You
Offering work experience can provide a talent pipeline for an employer, raise the profile of opportunities within a company and give scope for employees to develop their management skills.
In addition, young people offer new ideas and fresh ways of thinking, reflecting the interests and needs of the next generation of customers and consumers.
Ways of Supporting
As well as offering advice or work experience, there are plenty of other opportunities for OEs to help pupils, such as participating at the World of Work event for Year 11 pupils and the Work the Room evening for the Lower Sixth, or attending a professional networking event.
Seeking Careers Advice
Many of our OEs offer careers advice and work experience to pupils and graduates.
Sixth Form pupils and recent leavers are also encouraged to attend some of the many professional networking events held throughout the year.
There are also several LinkedIn groups OEs may join as follows:
Old Epsomian Club Official Group
OE Legal Society
OE Medical Society
OE Property & Financial Services Society
